SMTO-GML-0049 — The separate Gmail setup helper is no longer used

GUID: 5b281278-7aec-4d55-b6ad-5d694b5fb779
Slug: gmail-broker-retired
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The command you ran used to start a separate helper for connecting Gmail. SMTO now connects Gmail itself, so the command only shows this notice and does nothing else.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Stop running the gmail-broker command, and remove it from any script or startup routine that runs it. Running it again will only show this same notice; it no longer starts anything.
  2. In SMTO, select More options › Parameter Store and create an entry with the Gmail OAuth App template, using the client ID and secret from your Google Cloud project. SMTO now keeps your Google sign-in app details there instead of in the separate helper.
  3. In a conversation, ask SMTO to connect Gmail, for example 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app and save the account as work_gmail', and finish the sign-in in your browser. This is the supported way to link a Gmail account now.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports your Gmail account as connected and can search your email.

If it still fails

  • If connecting from the conversation shows a different error, follow that error's steps. Otherwise select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The retired aor gmail-broker CLI command printed this notice and exited; Gmail OAuth is now configured through Gmail OAuth App records in Parameter Store and the gmail.connect capability.

What this means

  • The CLI broker command emits the retired-broker diagnostic and directs setup to the supported Parameter Store OAuth App flow. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The CLI broker command emits the retired-broker diagnostic and directs setup to the supported Parameter Store OAuth App flow.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the invoked command and current supported Gmail connection entry point.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Stop invoking aor gmail-broker (its --host/--port options are ignored) and remove it from scripts or service units. Create a Gmail OAuth App record in Parameter Store (/parameter-editor) and connect accounts with gmail.connect from a conversation.

Retry and execution caution

  • The retired broker command cannot be made available by retrying it. Use the supported Gmail connection workflow.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account connects through its configured OAuth App and gmail.connect.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
